main_body: Snow-covered conifer: a stack of dark green foliage tiers, each capped with a snow layer, on a short brown trunk
top_band: Snow bands at the centre column: rows 12-15 (L 228, 200, 166) above green foliage from row 16; the same pattern repeats at rows 24-26, 33-35 and 44-46
evidence: The tree has no flat top, but each tier carries a multi-row light snow band (about 3-4 rows) that reads as a horizontal surface seen from above. Dark green foliage faces of 6-9 rows sit under each band, with a big step in lightness (L about 166 to 59 or below). The silhouette widens downward in tiers, and no isometric side face is drawn. For an organic piece this reads as 3/4.

style.evidence: The measured facts put the candidate far below both references: 9 colours per tile against 108-109, and 15 distinct colours against 427 and 567. Flat-fill coverage is 0% and the dark edge pixels are not neutral (0% near-neutral), so the outline is a tinted dark green, which is fine. The foliage uses only about 3-4 greens plus 3-4 snow tones, with little per-clump leaf texture and mostly blocky stepped tiers. Beside the richly clumped Beodeul canopies it looks thinner and flatter, so it fails on shading steps and tile density.
